html:
SMTO-UI-0042 — There are too many permission rules in one list

GUID: e4444fb8-508d-4918-9281-4ddd52a430cd
Slug: ui-permission-rule-limit
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Permission settings can hold up to 32 rules for Skills and up to 128 rules each for tools and for commands. One of these lists is full, so your new rule wasn't added. Your saved rules haven't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Permissions below the message box and look through the Skills, tools and Shell command permissions lists for rules you don't need. Each list has a maximum number of rules, so removing extras brings it back under the limit.
  2. Set each rule you don't need to Default. Then add the rule you wanted and select Apply. Choosing Default removes that rule, which frees a place in the list.
  3. Where many tools of one Skill share the same choice, set that once on the Skill and set its individual tools back to Default. One Skill rule covers all of its tools, so it takes fewer rules.

What success looks like

  • Apply closes the Permissions window without an error and your remaining rules show in the summary.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove the safety rules you rely on just to get under the limit; check with them first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Permission-policy validation rejected a rule family because it is not an array or exceeds its limit: 32 skill_rules, or 128 tool_rules or shell_rules.

What this means

  • A permission rule family is not an array or exceeds 32 Skill rules or 128 rules for another supported family. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A permission rule family is not an array or exceeds 32 Skill rules or 128 rules for another supported family.

How to diagnose it

  • Check each rule container's type and count independently.

How to fix it

  • permission_policy.js canonical() throws ui_permission_rule_limit when skill_rules, tool_rules or shell_rules is not an array or exceeds 32/128/128 entries (matching the Field max_length limits in permission_policy.py). Remove or consolidate rules, for example replace many tool rules with one Skill rule, and keep the policy within these limits.
  • Supply rule arrays within the limits: at most 32 Skill rules and 128 rules per other supported family.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each supported family is an array within its own bound.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
